claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co starting powder is a metastable BCC solid solution.
SPS at 900–980 °C precipitates a nanoscale Mg-depleted, (Al,Ti,V)-rich intermetallic network.
The precipitated intermetallic network enhances hardness.
The precipitated intermetallic network enhances bulk density.
The precipitated intermetallic network promotes formation of a protective oxide scale.
Temperatures above 1000 °C cause Mg volatility and compositional deviation.
Mg evaporation above 1000 °C introduces porosity.
Below 800 °C, diffusion is too slow to nucleate the secondary barrier phase during the SPS holding time.
An SPS regime of 900–980 °C, 30–50 MPa, and approximately 10–20 minutes under vacuum or inert gas is suitable for the proposed process.
The secondary phase is an (Al,Ti,V)-rich B2 or Laves-type phase located at grain boundaries and triple junctions as a continuous network.
High configurational entropy of the BCC matrix suppresses bulk intermetallic formation at lower temperatures.
A localized thermodynamic or kinetic driving force at grain boundaries during SPS at 900–980 °C triggers secondary-phase nucleation.
The secondary phase retards outward diffusion of Mg.
The secondary phase retards inward diffusion of oxygen.
The diffusion-barrier network prevents grain coarsening.
The proposed mechanism promotes a Cr/Al-rich passive oxide layer.
Material sintered in the proposed window will achieve greater than 95% theoretical density.
Material sintered in the proposed window will achieve Vickers hardness greater than 400 HV.
The corrosion current density will be one order of magnitude lower than for samples sintered at 800 °C or 1000 °C.
The passive film will have a bilayer structure with an Al/Ti-oxide-enriched inner barrier layer.

contradictions.description: The mechanism predicts a Cr/Al-rich passive oxide even though Cr is not a constituent of the stated Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co alloy.
The mechanism specifies a Cr/Al-rich passive layer, whereas the predicted outcome specifies an Al/Ti-enriched inner layer; the proposed passive-film chemistry is inconsistent.
The failure boundary is stated as temperatures exceeding 1000 °C, but the 1000 °C baseline itself is asserted to undergo Mg loss, porosity, and property degradation.
